newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says sent back 2,712 Albanian "undesirables".
newsitem.headline: Italy says sent back 2,712 Albanian "undesirables".

text.p: Italy said on Tuesday it had repatriated a total of 2,712 Albanian "undesirables" -- almost one fifth of all those who have fled to Italy to escape recent chaos in their impoverished Balkan state.
The Interior Ministry said in the past 10 days alone, 614 Albanians deemed unworthy of refugee status had been sent home.

That included more than half those who arrived in a dangerously overcrowded boat on April 27 and one quarter of the 1,229 Albanians -- the biggest boatload to date -- whose vessel limped into the southern port of Bari on Sunday.
More than 14,000 refugees have fled across the Adriatic to Italy since the collapse of fraudulent savings schemes sparked violent unrest and swept Albania into near anarchy in March.
The exodus prompted Italy's parliament to vote in favour of allowing genuine refugees to stay up to 90 days but to send back criminal elements and those just looking for a better lifestyle.

Opposition politicians have called for a crackdown on would-be immigrants and Interior Minister Giorgio Napolitano said earlier this week that those Albanians who were not fleeing because their lives were in danger would be sent back.
Italy has been bracing for more arrivals as defence sources have said thousands of Albanians may be camping out near beaches in the north awaiting more ships to ferry them across to Italy.
An Italian-led multinational security force in Albania to oversee the safe delivery of humanitarian aid has no authority to stop the flood of refugees.
